text:
miko: weird one 0min ago - following the "next-slim-rag" starter (Next13 + LlamaIndex) and notice KV-cache hits are reported in the UI but embeddings count in Console goes up for every request. seems like the sample is re-embedding on every call even when kv-hit is true.

miko: repro quick: clone github.com/redwood/samples/next-slim-rag && yarn dev, use starter dataset, run query twice -> UI shows cache hit on second run but Console embed_calls increments both times.

fran: do you have the exact handler? maybe the sample calls embed within the request path before checking cache?

miko: handler excerpt (api/qa.js):
```js
const existing = await kv.get(key);
if (!existing) {
  const emb = await Redwood.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-1', input: text });
  await kv.set(key, emb);
}
const answer = await Redwood.call({ model: 'llama-7b', input: query });
```
looks fine. UI shows existing=true on second call though.

fran: two possibilities: 1) the UI checks a local kv (client-side) while the server is re-embedding, 2) the embedding call is happening in middleware or a background function the starter triggers (like a freshness job). any background hooks in the sample?

miko: none in the repo. i added console.log around the kv.get and it returns non-null before the embedding line executes, but embedding still runs 1ms later. looks racey.

devrel: could be the SDK's batching middleware. earlier SDK versions had an optimization that opportunistically enqueued embeddings for batch. if kv.get is synchronous-ish but embedding batch handler sees the request as missing due to a different cache namespace, it might dedupe poorly. which SDK version?

miko: @devrel using "@redwood/inference-js": "0.11.2" (template pinned).

fran: check if the sample uses different cache keys for read vs write (typo) or if TTL is 0. also check if kv.set is async but not awaited in some code path; your snippet awaits it though. any middleware modifying headers that cause the embed call to route to a fallback model which doesn't match cached vector signature?

miko: digging: there's a tiny helper in /lib/embeds.js that normalizes the input and calls `await Redwood.embeddings.create(...)`. i added logging and observed: on second request, kv.get returns object with vector but embed call still fires and returns a vector identical to the cached one. interestingly the embedding call goes to a different model id during the second call: first call model: embed-1, second call model: embed-1--v2 (the sample has a model aliasing map). Console shows both calls as embed_calls to different model ids.

devrel: aha. that explains it. the cache key was computed from the input and original model alias, but the runtime alias resolver swapped in v2 for the second call (we rolled out aliasing update in infra yesterday). the starter computed key with canonical name `embed-1` but the SDK resolved to `embed-1--v2` on call path. result: cache misses.

miko: how did infra rename alias on us? we didn't pin model names in the starter.

fran: every sample should compute cache keys using the SDK's resolved model identity or include the model alias version in the key material. two fixes: 1) pin model id in starter config (recommended), or 2) use SDK helper `Redwood.embeddings.keyFor({model, input})` (we should add this helper) so key includes canonical resolver.

ops-bot: infra note: alias rollout caused transparent redirect to v2 for minor perf fixes. we should add an advisory in samples release notes when aliases change. created infra task ALIAS-908.

miko: immediate patch: pin embed model to exact id in sample config and add README note to highlight model aliasing can invalidate caches. added a small warning in the UI dev banner: "If you see KV hits in UI but embeddings increasing in Console, ensure model id pinned or use SDK key helper."

devrel: also adding a lint rule to sample scaffolds to fail if model value includes a non-fixed alias token (regex match for `--v\d`). and we'll add a unit test that simulates alias swap to ensure cache keys are stable.

fran: follow-up: can we make SDK expose canonical model id synchronously so cache code doesn't need to call network? we can compute stable key by hashing the input plus the declared model id; if aliasing changes we still need to consider alias version. maybe better to require explicit model pin.

miko: opened PR 3347 in samples with pin + README + dev banner. linked to infra/ALIAS-908.

ops-bot: created issue #1805 (devex) "starter: model aliasing invalidates KV caches" and linked PR 3347.

miko: thanks all! learned: pin models for starters, and check model ids in Console when cache mismatch shows up.
